sigma_analysis_results.rule_description:
Detects execution of the "finger.exe" utility.
Finger.EXE or "TCPIP Finger Command" is an old utility that is still present on modern Windows installation. It Displays information about users on a specified remote computer (typically a UNIX computer) that is running the finger service or daemon.
Due to the old nature of this utility and the rareness of machines having the finger service. Any execution of "finger.exe" can be considered "suspicious" and worth investigating.

crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The binary is a benign implementation of the 'finger' network utility. Its primary function, `netfinger`, uses standard Windows Sockets (Winsock) APIs like `GetAddrInfoW`, `socket`, and `connect` to query a remote host. It specifically resolves the service name "finger" (port 79/tcp) and sends a request, then prints the response. Descriptive strings like "finger - finger command line tools." and the command-line argument parsing in `wmain` confirm its intended purpose as a standard network tool.
